Mapping the 8 consumer-less key types is canon by test_key_graph.py:58-62's own words ('guessing one is exactly the fabrication this repo's no-fabrication rule forbids'), and single-ownering the contested CI scalar adjudicates between TWO CANONICAL docs (ci_political and territorial_piety) -- a canon decision wearing engine clothes. title: Seven-lens read-only world-churn audit: the churn machinery is built and DISCONNECTED, not scripted; eight decisions held for Jordan
description: Seven independent Fable-5 read-only lenses over the executable model (A Key substrate/propagation core, B cross-scale transport, C world tracks/clocks/threshold events, D NPCs/convictions/threadwork/arcs, E factions/settlements/mass battle, F scene-subsystem writeback, G prior art) asking how Key-substrate state changes over a campaign and whether the primitives compose into emergent conditions reaching NPCs, arcs and events. HEADLINE: the world does not churn because the machinery is DISCONNECTED, not because it is scripted -- three lenses reached this independently. The anti-scripting-drift guardrail HELD: exactly one entity-hardcoding instance was found across seven lenses (pr119_event_deck_engine.py:74-75,115) and it sits in the zero-caller sim_harness cluster. Scenes ARE seeded from live world state, not templates (scene_dispatch.py:92-93,135-138). WHAT CHURNS: three closed loops (parliamentary spine; territory<->CI; conquest<->signals) plus real autonomous drift (CI +1/season, MS -1/year, NPE stance, per-season stochastic faction actions). Factions DO act autonomously (mc_v18.py:124-130). WHAT CANNOT: (D1) the insurgency pipeline is emergent, implemented, invoked every season and STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE -- no code path anywhere sets Territory.owner = None, so mc_v18.py:298's insurgencies_formed is always 0; promotion is doubly dead (needs L>=3, records start at 1.0, nothing mutates L). Found independently by lenses C and E. (D2) victory.py:73 reads Turmoil, nothing writes Turmoil -- a victory leg that can never fail, the SS0.1-point-2 defect class. (D3) the Stability-Crisis council writes L but triggers on Sta, so it refires identically every season instead of compounding. (D4) battle casualties evaporate (massbattle.py:1850-1851 computed, never applied) and Faction.Mil is a monotone ratchet with only the 7.0 ceiling as brake. (D5) ZERO person-scale state changes in a seeded campaign -- conviction/beliefs/coherence/knots are real and correctly wired but every producer is a stub, and the world-event -> Key -> person path TERMINATES AT THE KEY (no code applies impact_vector or stat_deltas to any person store). (D6) a live correctness bug: apply_knot_loss passes conviction='Loyalty', absent from CONVICTIONS, so apply_conviction_scar returns magnitude=0 while the caller reports conviction_scar=1. (D7) the Key substrate is a telemetry spine, not the churn engine: 3 of 55 types emit, one closes a loop, cascades are IMPOSSIBLE (DEFAULT_CASCADE_DEPTH_MAX=0), 10 of 13 subscriptions have no producer. (D8) top-down Key delivery has zero emitters; test_pipeline_reach.py:427-440 proves direction 4 by REUSING a bottom-up key. (D11) arcs are generated from documents, not churn, by a skill whose read paths (params/) and output target (arcs/simulated/) were BOTH evacuated 2026-08-05 -- following it as written would recreate a do-not-recreate tree. PRIOR ART: the churn engine was RATIFIED 2026-07-05 (ED-IN-0011) and almost none of it landed; two things rotted underneath it -- the 138-arc corpus its L0 compile calibrates against was evacuated (so the ratified compile cannot run as specified) while an UNRATIFIED proposal (settlement_generator_v1.md:127) claims the L0 slot, and spec/churn_amendments.md, a ratified normative companion, no longer resolves (its content sits inside a file banner-marked 'Not independently ratifiable' while CURRENT.md:165 still cites the dead path). DELIVERABLE: audit/2026-08-08-world-churn-audit/{00_findings,01_plan}.md -- a defect register ordered by leverage-per-unit-of-new-design, and a plan whose Tier 0 is correctness/guards/instruments (each shipping its falsifier), Tier 1 is the few edges that light up already-built machinery (flag-gated OFF, goldens byte-exact), Tier 2 is substrate maturation, and Tier 3 is EIGHT DECISIONS HELD FOR JORDAN (J-A the L0 identity fork, J-B insurgency L growth rule, J-C conviction vocabulary reconciliation across 3 dialects, J-D ED-1051 engine_clock, J-E Strain/Turmoil/PI key collapse, J-F council->Sta direction/magnitude, J-G the unresolvable ratified churn_amendments companion, J-H the arc-generator skill's evacuated paths). NOTHING EXECUTED: no canonical head moved, no design text changed, no flag flipped, no golden re-recorded. MERGING THIS PR RATIFIES NONE OF TIER 3 -- flagged loudly per the ED-1094 exception rule. Adversarial review by two independent read-only critics (fidelity + plan logic) was IN FLIGHT at commit time; their verdicts, including anything they overturn, land as a follow-up commit. Weakest claims carried honestly: the counts and absence-claims rest on grep with the known dynamic-access blind spot and NO guard test pins them -- which is precisely what plan item T0-4 (the connectivity instrument) exists to fix.

title: World-schema gap audit: three method-disjoint interrogations of the entity ladder, 18 domain lenses and the individuation surface against the Key registry + module contracts
description: INSTRUMENT + METHOD RECORD (this entry; the findings register lands separately). The corpus measures what is BUILT exhaustively -- ENGINE_ATLAS section 2 declared-vs-executed, the 15 flow-skeleton section 7 gap lists, the KEY_INDEX/CONTRACT_INDEX review queues -- and nowhere asks systematically what the world model REQUIRES that the schema cannot express. The schema is exactly two authored surfaces (key_type_registry_v30.md, 55 types; module_contracts.yaml, 27 modules); everything in references/ that renders them is a generated VIEW, where a blank cell means 'not declared' and NOT 'none'. Three orthogonal decompositions of one subject, none seeing the others' output: A/Strata walks the ratified entity ladder rung by rung (4 lanes); B/Lenses sweeps 18 domain lenses across every rung at once (5 lanes); C/Config asks what must be AUTHORED for an instance to be unique, consequential and legible (3 lanes) -- a distinct class of question, since a world of 37 near-identical settlements and 4 stat-block factions emits keys perfectly and produces no narrative. A gap reached from two different passes is corroborated by disjoint METHOD, which is the ED-IN-0152 verification pattern applied prospectively rather than retrospectively. Antagonist half is structural, not declared: 4 critics route through hCritic() -> valoria-critic (tools: Read, Grep, Glob), receive producer OUTPUT and never producer reasoning, and are handed rediscovery groups rather than an arbitrary slice. THREE FACTS MEASURED BY HAND before the run, each load-bearing on its design. (1) CORRECTED IN-SESSION BY JORDAN, 2026-08-11: **characters ARE NPCs** -- there is no PC/NPC distinction in Valoria, so the character entity is the NPC dataclass in systems/world/sim/npe.py, and the earlier framing of this entry ('no Character class exists anywhere') was a true statement about class NAMES that implied a false conclusion about the MODEL. The measured fact survives the correction and sharpens under it: no module_contracts.yaml row and no key_type_registry family OWNS character identity -- all 27 modules treat npc_id/actor_id as an opaque foreign key -- and the identity is recorded twice at two scales with no bridge, NPC.territory_id at the province grain versus Settlement.npc_ids, with no settlement_id on the character anywhere. Lane A1 reached that framing independently, without the correction, which is why the run is not invalidated by it. (2) The contracts scales enum is 7-valued with no 'national', while scale_hierarchy_v1.md is Jordan-ratified at Country > Duchy > Province > Territory > Settlement -- a ladder the schema cannot name. (3) key_type_registry section 10 (RATIFIED 2026-07-07, ED-IN-0026) forbids appending any new key type without a row in references/rendering_dispositions.yaml, WHICH DOES NOT EXIST, so this audit proposes keys and does not append any. CORRECTED 2026-08-11 by the register's own G-17 row and a second-pass adversarial review: 'structurally cannot append' is TOO STRONG. Section 10 :1287-1291 has A15 enforce the precondition REPORT-ONLY against the existing 55-type roster first, flipping to blocking only 'once rendering_dispositions.yaml exists and the backlog is at zero'. Appends today are GOVERNED AND UNRECORDED, not mechanically refused. The real obligation is that every propose_key row ships its rendering-disposition row as a co-artifact, plus regeneration of the GENERATED engine/engine_params/key_types.json export. That blockage is a register row, not an obstacle to route around. RATIFIES NOTHING and is called out as held back in full under the ED-1094 exception: no head moves, no status flips, no contract or registry is edited. Scope stops honoured: no renames (the dotted-namespace proposal is HELD, ED-IN-0152) and no scale-vocabulary unification (HELD at ED-IN-0103 fork 1) -- lanes RECORD those seams where they hit them.

title: hRediscover's grouping precondition zeroes the corroboration signal it exists to compute — found by the ED-IN-0153 run, in that run's own instrument
description: MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. The ED-IN-0153 world-schema gap audit ran 12 producer lanes across three method-disjoint passes specifically so that a gap reached by lanes from different passes would carry an independent-rediscovery signal. hRediscover returned 75 groups from 75 findings: every rediscovery value was 1. The signal was not weak, it was absent, and the synthesis stage silently reconstructed it by hand from lane labels and claim wording -- which is the worst of both outcomes, because the returned object still carries a rediscovery column that reads as measured. ROOT CAUSE: hSameFinding gates on hFirstFile(a) === hFirstFile(b) BEFORE comparing content words, and hFirstFile returns the first file-shaped token in a finding's free-text evidence string. Two lanes describing one gap from different directions rarely lead with the same citation, so the file-equality precondition zeroed the comparison before the fuzzy matcher ever ran. THE OWNER PREDICTED THIS FAILURE AND THEN INHERITED IT. tools/wf_harness.js's own comment on the exact key says: 'An exact key splits them into singletons and silently zeroes out the entire corroboration signal, which is worse than not computing it: the output still has a rediscovery column, it just always reads 1.' hSameFinding was written as the remedy for precisely that and kept the same-file precondition, so it reproduces the defect for any finding shape whose evidence is multi-citation free text. Section 0.1 point-5 signature: correct for the shape it was written against, silently wrong for the shape that arrived later. SCOPE: NOT FIXED HERE. The owner is copied verbatim into every .claude/wf_*.js, its behaviour is pinned by tests/valoria/test_wf_harness.py (mutation-verified 13/13), and the grouping rule needs its own expected-delta test rather than a drop-in edit -- widening an audit PR into a harness change is the scope creep section 0.1 point 5 warns about. Filed for its own pass. ED-IN-0153's orchestration plan section 6 predicted this limit as 'a floor, never a ceiling -- it under-reports corroboration and cannot over-report it'. That prediction is FALSIFIED in the direction that matters: it did not under-report, it reported nothing. The correction is recorded in audit/2026-08-11-world-schema-gap-audit/02_verdict_and_residuals.md section 2.
falsifier: THE GUARD IS THE DELIVERABLE, NOT THE PATCH. Any fix must ship with a test that fails when two findings describing one defect through DIFFERENT first-cited files collapse to two singletons -- i.e. a fixture of two paraphrases citing different files must group to rediscovery 2. Without that test the pattern recurs invisibly, which is exactly what happened here: the existing suite is green and mutation-verified, and did not catch it, because it pins that signal() never throws and that a tripped run still returns a summary -- not that grouping groups. Reproduce the defect now: the ED-IN-0153 run returned raw_findings 75 / distinct_gaps 75 with rediscovery_top all 1s.

Commit dates were NOT checked and neither reading is asserted; that is the open item. Either way the guard is the same. Related class: a dated measurement in prose with nothing that fails when it drifts (cf. CLAUDE.md's duplicated date, ED-IN-0147) -- occurring here INSIDE a guard file. It is filed rather than silently corrected because the ED-IN-0153 audit repeated the stale figure before measuring it. The adjacent '16 direct Python imports' and '47 dotted key names' figures in the same docstring were NOT re-measured and must not be cited without measuring. NOT FIXED HERE: correcting the sentence without adding the guard would reproduce the defect on the next keying wave.
falsifier: The guard is the deliverable, not the edited sentence. A test must COMPUTE live emit coverage -- count distinct type_ids constructed at real sched.emit() call sites -- and fail when the number changes without the recorded figure changing with it, in the manner of the existing KNOWN_NO_PRODUCER/KNOWN_NO_CONSUMER ratchet in the same file, which is the correct local pattern to compose on. description: 'KEY CONTRACTS AND MODULE CONTRACTS ETC NEED TO BE EXPLICITLY DEFINED IN A CENTRALIZED HIERARCHICAL MANNER' (Jordan, this session) — RULED, NOT EXECUTED, AND LOGGED LATE. Like ED-FA-0038 this ruling went unrecorded: a post-merge audit grepped the tree for its own words and found ZERO files. It is filed `status: open` and NOT `needs_jordan` — Jordan has ruled; what is missing is execution, and flagging it for him would be the parking-space misuse CLAUDE.md 0 forbids. THE MEASURED CURRENT STATE, so the next session starts from a fact rather than an impression. Three registries exist and none of them is hierarchically related to the others: references/module_contracts.yaml (27 modules + 27 composition_roles, with each module's Key IN -> resolver -> OUT and owned state), engine/engine_params/key_types.json (55 key types, cooked from key_type_registry_v30.md behind a blocking exporter), and references/descriptor_registry.yaml (attributes, aggregates, faction/settlement stats and their bounds). They are three FLAT namespaces that reference each other by string. There is no single surface from which a reader — or the Godot port — can descend from 'the game' to a subsystem to a module to its Keys to the fields those Keys carry. WHY IT IS NOT DONE HERE, stated rather than left as an unexplained gap: it is a genuine architecture job, not a re-siting. It needs a decision about what the hierarchy's LEVELS are (scale? subsystem? module? Key?), whether the existing three registries become views of one artifact or stay separate with a declared parent, and what the exporter/round-trip story is for the composite. Faking it by nesting the current three files under a new top-level key would produce a hierarchy in shape and not in meaning, which is worse than the honest flat state because it would look done. WHAT IS ALREADY POINTING THIS WAY, and should be read before starting: systems/_architecture/propagation_spec_v1.md 1's O.2 engine_clock contract is the worked example of a module contract stated properly; ED-1051 is the open question of whether that form is ratified; 9 of 27 modules still carry `doc: null` and 11 of 27 resolvers are [ASSUMPTION]-grade, so a third of the contract surface is not yet an implementable spec at all. A hierarchy over a surface that incomplete would centralise the holes as much as the content. Authoring the missing contracts is plausibly the first half of this work. RELATED AND DELIBERATELY SEPARATE: the wrapper/orchestrator architecture Jordan described in the same conversation (each subsystem has a wrapper handling all Key I/O; inputs trickle down with increasing granularity, outputs aggregate up) is the RUNTIME half of the same idea. ED-SC-0032 executed one instance of it — the degree-ladder extension seam — and that is one seam, not the architecture. MEASURED-BY: references/module_contracts.yaml - the 27 modules and 27 composition roles, and the `doc: null` / [ASSUMPTION] grades that bound how much of it is specifiable today. PERSONNEL PRECONDITION — RULED BY JORDAN, THIS SESSION, NOT EXECUTED. Verbatim: 'all faction actions, settlement governance, mass battles, etc are predicated upon people existing. we do not allow the game to perform faction actions if there is no leader of that faction, and that leader themselves is going to influence what choices are made for available faction actions in the same way that the person(s) who are governing a settlement or conducting a battle may make different choices with the same information and options.' Filed status:open and NOT needs_jordan — Jordan has ruled; what is missing is execution. TWO CLAUSES, and they are separable. (1) THE GATE: no leader, no faction action; no governor, no settlement governance; no commander, no battle (the third is the one genuine ambiguity — see below). (2) THE DECIDER: the person shapes WHICH action is chosen from the same option set with the same information. Clause 2 is presence-as-identity, not presence-as-a-stat: the person must change the choice, not scale a modifier. MEASURED STATE AT HEAD. engine/autoload/game_state.py Faction has NO leader/ruler/head field (verified by read, :109-140). engine/mc_v18.py's faction pass gates on exactly two conditions, `faction.parliamentary` and `faction.territories`, then calls faction_action unconditionally. systems/factions/sim/faction_action.py selects with one rng.random() against a prior re-weighted by three RNG-free FACTION-level signals; no person is consulted anywhere. Settlement.governor_id is None on all 37 after world-gen and its only writer succeed_governor has zero callers. massbattle.py's _faction_to_unit sets neither charisma nor cognition, so derive_command falls back to a hardcoded command=4 despite COMMAND_SIGMA_ENABLED defaulting ON. world.npcs is empty in every seeded campaign. THE BOOTSTRAP CONSEQUENCE, which is the load-bearing one: under clause 1, with world.npcs empty, a campaign performs ZERO faction actions. The ruling therefore promotes the person loader from an enhancement to a PRECONDITION OF THE ENGINE RUNNING, and requires leaders to exist at world-gen before season 1 rather than being generated during play. SECOND CONSEQUENCE: it makes systems/social_contest/sim/contest/faction.py::succession load-bearing. That within-faction two-claimant contest is currently unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION because Faction has no leader field; under this ruling a faction with no viable successor stops acting, which gives faction collapse a mechanism it presently lacks. THIRD CONSEQUENCE: the deciding logic belongs to a person-AI, not a faction-AI. engine/autoload/npc_ai.py is the module named for it; both its entry points are typed no-ops and its docstring names faction_action as a DEPENDENCY, which is backwards under this ruling. NERS NOTE: clause 2 must not be implemented as a flat trait bonus on the selection roll. A flat shift is worth Dz = X/(0.8*sqrt(Pool)) and so is worth more to a small pool — the flat-shift trap. The in-band implementation is that the leader changes the OPTION SET and the POOL SOURCE, not a modifier: surveyed precedent gates on class (Total War: Three Kingdoms) rather than scaling. ONE GENUINE AMBIGUITY, flagged rather than decided: 'no commander, no battle' has two readings that lead to different games — (a) a faction with no available commander CANNOT declare a conquest, or (b) it can, and an unled army fights at a penalty (the Dominions shape). (a) is a gate consistent with clause 1; (b) is a modifier and re-opens the leverage question. Recorded as open. IMPACT CLASS: MOVES, at the largest scale in the tree — it changes which actions occur, so every seeded golden moves and a balance_oracle control is mandatory. title: Fan-out off `total` — R7 executed in the season loop (19_PLAN.md step 1 / 21_RECONCILIATION.md PHASE 1 step 2)
summary: THE DEFAULT `fan_out_mode` MOVES `total` -> `all_five` IN `engine/season/data/fixtures.py`. `total` fans every Event to every person, which is R7's ECHO MODEL arriving at the deposit layer: nothing is hideable, so there is no secret, no lie, no rumour, and no such thing as being absent. R7 ruled the architecture model — legitimacy falls where the news has reached. `total` stays as H-33's control arm and #353 S61's specified behaviour; the channel list is untouched (19_PLAN.md step 1: do not touch the arm set). H-33 STAYS `assumption`: R7 rules which arm DOES NOT ship -- between `presence_only` and `all_five` the ruling is SILENT and that choice was made on measurement, not by ruling -- and it says nothing about what the five predicates are. ⚠ The grade's WEIGHT changed even though the grade did not: under `total` the predicates were never consulted; under `all_five` they decide every deposit. MEASURED, build_world(0), 3 seasons: deposits 649 -> 60; ledgers [200,200,200] -> [0,28,32]; questions raised 5/9/10 -> 5/9/10 at `all_five` and 5/8/8 at `presence_only`, which is why the arm is `all_five`. CONTROL, AND IT IS WEAKER THAN THE FIRST WRITING OF THIS ENTRY CLAIMED: 122 probes re-run, ZERO verdict changes (63 PASS / 59 GAP either side), and their measured DETAILS moved substantially (A28's event count 7,836 -> 127, W6's plague reaching 35 ledgers -> 9, A5's log content hash). But probe and case verdicts resolve partly against register `grade:` cells rather than run behaviour (`harness/exercises.py:275-280`: `absent` blocks, `assumption` passes as assumed, `ruled`/`measured` pass), and two probes pin `fan_out_mode` themselves. So this is a MODERATE control -- the probes executed and nothing flipped -- not the strong one labelling it `CONTROL:` implied. Found by the adversarial pass. ARTIFACT: two persons' witness-deposit sets are IDENTICAL under `total` (0 differing pairs) and differ under the shipped arm — the first secret in the world, pinned with the `total` control inside the same test. ⚠ M-6 CANNOT FAIL AS SPECIFIED and is not reported as passed: `_r3_propagates` walks Event.causes[] over driver.resolved and never reads a ledger, so the corpus tallies (NPC R3 30/30, ARC 54/59) are identical across all three arms both co-located AND dispersed to distinct rungs. What is claimed is narrower: links 1 and 2 of the claim->question->act chain survive the flip. ⛔ THE COST IS LARGER THAN THE FIRST WRITING OF THIS ENTRY SAID, AND THE ARGUMENT THAT DISCOUNTED IT IS REFUTED. That writing called it a 16-fork artifact and cited H-54's hash-ordering share (801 of 1,068) as why 16 forks cannot rank the arms. TWO ERRORS, both found by an adversarial pass. (a) 801/1,068 was measured at fan_out_mode=total and cited to justify leaving total — wd_acceptance.fixtures_for never sweeps fan_out_mode. Re-run at all_five: 801 of 1,068, IDENTICAL in all six cells, with 39 of 108 fields moved so the re-run was no no-op. The number survives; citing it unrun did not. (b) The corpus-scale control existed, chunked and ready, and was not run. Run now — 89 worlds, 1,467 genuine forks, narrow cell, at observation_deposit_mode `actor`: total 62 of 1467 (95.77% reconvergence) · all_five 0 of 1467 (100.00%) · presence_only 229 of 1467 (84.39%). ZERO OF 1,467 IS NOT A SLICE ARTIFACT. At the SHIPPED arm a fork never changes a later decision, and presence_only — rejected here on a 2-question difference in one 3-person world — is nearly 4x the pre-flip arm. ⭐⭐ AND THE ZERO IS NOW DIAGNOSED, WHICH RETIRES THE ARM QUESTION RATHER THAN ANSWERING IT. A fork reaches a later decision by exactly ONE route: §F1 clause 4 (shape.py:627, belief_contradicts). Counting that population over the same 89 worlds (wd_extra.corpus_drops) at observation_deposit_mode `actor`: total 37 drops / 62 divergences · all_five 0 / 0 · presence_only 114 / 229. THE DIVERGENCES TRACK THE DROPS EXACTLY, so the zero is neither a property of the arm nor a channel defect — clause 4 never fires at the shipped configuration and a fork has nothing to change. Beliefs still form there (22 false-when-recorded) and contradict nothing. ⭐ EVERY CLAUSE-4 DROP IN THE WHOLE CORPUS, IN EVERY CELL, IS THE VERB `move` REFUSING ON A `contain.path:<person>` BELIEF — *there is no road from here to there*, formed by witnessing travel.blocked and overturned by a later travel.moved. Nothing else fires clause 4 at all. So the metric measures PEOPLE BEING WRONG, and a wider channel set does not suppress propagation: it CORRECTS THE STALE BELIEF BEFORE IT CAN BITE. ⚠ THE ARM IS THEREFORE NOT CHOSEN ON IT IN EITHER DIRECTION — a monoculture of one verb and one predicate, and tuning the knowledge layer to preserve `move`'s refusals would protect a single worked instance. THE DEFECT EXPOSED IS THAT §F1 CLAUSE 4 HAS EXACTLY ONE REACHABLE INSTANCE IN THE CORPUS, a producer hole and the place the work goes. The shipped arm stays 19_PLAN.md step 1's, which is also the only arm producing a secret between two co-located people. NON-MONOTONIC in the channel set, since all_five is a superset of presence_only. Half the channel survives: under the widened (verb, subject) fingerprint `actor` still diverges 8 against the control's 6 (was 11 against 7), so W-B still changes what a person deliberates ABOUT and no longer changes the verb set. The arm is NOT re-chosen on it, per CLAUDE.md §0 tests 3 and 5: 19_PLAN.md step 1 names the channel-predicate arm, and H-54 registers that within-source question order is decided by lexicographic order over content hashes in 801 of 1,068 deliberations, so a 16-fork slice supports no ranking of the arms. ⚠ AND ONE REGISTERED ARGUMENT EXPIRED: the ledger cap now evicts NOTHING in any arm (48/49/204 -> 0/0/0), so H-122's first reason for defaulting to `actor` — that `total` flattens H-40 — is gone. ⛔ AND ITS SECOND REASON IS ALSO GONE, which a first writing of this entry got wrong: form 6 IS `claim.held`, and `LEDGER_DERIVED_STEMS` excludes that stem at the deposit site UNCONDITIONALLY (`shape.py:3789`), so `total` cannot put a holder-relative value in any ledger. That leg died 2026-09-04 with the W-B exclusion, BEFORE R7. So `actor`-over-`total` rests on NEITHER stated reason; the default is still not moved, because that would be a second design change riding a measurement in flux. Recorded on the row.

JORDAN'S VERB-TABLE RULINGS OF 2026-09-10, plus ONE OPEN FORK HE RAISED. Filed because these are design rulings made in session and this repository has no context between sessions; the plan is reference under section 0.05, so a ruling recorded only there is weak. RULING 1 -- VERBS ARE NOT FIATS. Verbatim: 'verbs invoke mechanisms or interactions between a character and another entity/character. they are not fiats.' This is the root of which the two HIGH findings against U7 group 1 were symptoms (see ED-IN-0206 and the R-execution plan section 15.0a): a fiat needs no counterparty, so nothing checked that the object of an `oblige` was an entity (it was not -- `einhir_texts` is a Proposition's subject FIELD, in none of persons/offices/rungs/records/sites/propositions); a fiat needs no two distinct parties, so a Tenure(X,X) self-loop read as lawful; a fiat cannot fail on the world's terms; a fiat is monotonic, which is why adding two verbs REDUCED measured divergence in all three fan-out arms. CONSEQUENCE: a real interaction has a COUNTERPARTY, an OBSTACLE and a DEGREE, and the ANTONYM is the fourth face -- what a fiat cannot do is be undone by another party's act. So U1 (obstacle, degree) is UPSTREAM of U7, not parallel: verbs built before them can only be fiats. RULING 2 -- THE ANTONYM ROSTER. Seven verbs create state nothing can destroy. Jordan named six closers: `oblige` <-> WAIVE; `succeed` <-> DEPOSED; `tie / knot` <-> FRAY / LOOSEN; `issue` <-> RESCIND; `petition` <-> WITHDRAW (petitioner) or DENY (receiver); `establish` <-> ABOLISH / DISSOLVE. The seventh, `utter` -> Proposition.exists, is DELIBERATELY unpaired: section 14 makes a Proposition immutable. NONE of the six closers exists in verb_table.yaml -- they are NEW ROWS, not unbuilt ones, which is why `grep release` finds nothing and 04_CODE_ARCHITECTURE.md:945's generic `release` is unbuilt. `petition`'s pair is TWO-SIDED (withdraw and deny close the same state from opposite sides), the first in the set where a counterparty is structurally required. RULING 3 -- 'the six investigation acts' IS NOT A VERB, and this is a live defect not a naming quibble. verb_table.yaml:490 carries it as a single row with `requires: 'per act'` and `writes: []`; it loads as a real VERB_TABLE key. Its own requires_typed_note admits it: 'the cell defers to six acts the table does not carry as rows'. CONSEQUENCE: len(VERB_TABLE) == 32 IS A FALSE DENOMINATOR -- 31 real verbs plus one placeholder standing for six unwritten rows, so the true count is 37 -- and the placeholder can never execute (no writes, no evaluable precondition, no effect), so it permanently inflates every ratio. Asserted at corpus_run.py:516, probes.py:988, test_season_shape.py:8374 (`assert len(VERB_TABLE) == 32`) and requirements.yaml R-05's measured line. LAYER 1 ALREADY NAMED THE REPAIR: HANDOFF_NEXT.md:55 item 2b -- 'split into six rows with writes; #359's discovery model (a contest of capability against secrecy, emitting a Degree) is the shape' -- which is exactly ruling 1's counterparty+obstacle+degree. AND ONE LAYER-1 CONTRADICTION TO SETTLE: PLAN.md:101 grades them assumption because they 'are UNNAMED... nothing to inject'. THEY ARE NAMED, in a CANONICAL doc: investigation_systems_v30.md:217 and :427 -- Examine, Interview, Research, Surveil, Thread-Read, Reconstruct. That premise is stale. THE OPEN FORK (needs_jordan) -- ARE `dispatch` AND `comply` TWO SIDES OF ONE THING? Jordan asked; it is not settled here. The table has TWO command channels and only one has responses: `issue` (remit:issue) writes Dispensation.exists and is answered by comply/evade-defy/refract, while `dispatch` (remit:dispatch) writes NOTHING, emits `order.given`, and has NO response verb -- its note reads 'it names a person; their own choose decides'. THE STRUCTURAL OBSERVATION THAT MAKES THIS a real fork: comply's precondition is 'a claim of the dispensation's terms is in the actor's own LEDGER' (section F.24a form 6), and that mechanism is ARTIFACT-AGNOSTIC -- `dispatch` emits order.given, which the witness channel deposits as a claim like any event. So comply could already answer a dispatch; the only thing preventing it is that the requires prose names the dispensation specifically. The response family is anchored to the ARTIFACT when the mechanism it runs on is the CLAIM. (a) ONE ACT AT TWO GRANULARITIES: personal order vs institutional rule, so comply/evade/refract key on the ledger claim and answer both; dispatch's missing response is a gap. (b) DISTINCT POWERS: separate remit keys, separate writes, separate emissions, so dispatch needs its own obey/disobey pair and comply stays with dispensations. Evidence leans (a) -- the mechanism is already shared and the remit split is about WHO MAY COMMAND, not what obeying is -- but it changes whether `comply` is one verb or two, which is a call about what the game means. NOT ESCALATED BY DEFAULT: it survives section 0's five tests because two defensible options lead to materially different games. ===== RENUMBERED ON MERGE, 2026-09-10. description: ED-IN-0210'S OPEN FORK ANSWERED: 'ARE dispatch AND comply TWO SIDES OF ONE THING?' -- NO. They are one PRODUCER and one member of the RESPONSE TRIAD, and the pair that is genuinely two-sided is dispatch/issue. Answered under CLAUDE.md section 0 gate 5 (where gates 1-4 are silent but one option is clearly right for the code, TAKE IT and record the reasoning) rather than escalated, and JORDAN MAY OVERTURN IT -- it is recorded here with its mechanism so that overturning it is cheap. THE MECHANISM, READ OFF THE VERB TABLE RATHER THAN ARGUED: comply.requires is 'a claim of the dispensation's terms is in the actor's own ledger' and comply.requires_typed is `none`, so the precondition asks for A CLAIM, NOT A CARRIER -- it is ARTIFACT-AGNOSTIC. evade / defy and refract both read `requires: as comply`, so all three response verbs key off the same claim. dispatch.requires is 'the named person exists', it writes nothing, and it emits `order.given`. WITNESS deposits a Claim whose PREDICATE IS THE EVENT KIND for every event with no per-kind allowlist (loop/witness.py:137 -- `c = Claim(cid, pid, subj, e.kind, ...)`), so `order.given` reaches observers' ledgers by the same path every other event does. THEREFORE dispatch already produces the precondition comply already reads, and no fold, no new verb and no schema change is required to join them. WHAT THE TWO PRODUCERS ACTUALLY DIFFER IN, and it is worth keeping: `issue` writes Dispensation.exists, so a formal order leaves a CARRIER -- inspectable, and a Record can be forged, destroyed or expire. `dispatch` writes nothing, so an informal order leaves only a CLAIM -- degradable by MATTER's confidence decay, deniable by its giver, and lost when the holder forgets it (AX-5 motion 3). An order you can deny having given versus an order that is on the books is a real distinction, and under the R2 properties (dynamic, capable, flexible, emergent, persistent) folding the two DELETES it. That is why gate 5 fires: one option is clearly right for the code AND strictly more capable. ⚠ THE ANSWER UNBLOCKS NOTHING IMMEDIATELY, AND SAYING SO IS PART OF THE ANSWER. comply has no effect body and `requires_typed: none`, so nothing evaluates its precondition mechanically -- that is H-72 class work, not this fork. And `dispatch` is one of H-71's five verbs no person can FORM (remit: is unevaluable person-side), so a ruling here moves no run until H-71 closes. Same relationship v7 section 1 records between M1 row 1 and OI-05: the ruling is not the blocker. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE QUEUE: ED-IN-0210 carried the last live Jordan-gated half of its row. With Rulings 1 and 2 re-sorted to WORK by ED-IN-0218 and the fork answered here, the row is fully disposed and workplans/2026-09-11-arc-sequence-spine.md:57's 'do not schedule it until ruled' no longer holds. FALSIFIER, per CLAUDE.md 0.1 pt 3: the claim that dispatch's event reaches a ledger is falsified if WITNESS filters deposits by event kind. It does not -- the deposit line takes `e.kind` unconditionally and the only skip in that loop is LEDGER_DERIVED_STEMS on the W-B observation deposit, which is a different branch. Add an allowlist to witness.py and this ruling's mechanism is gone.

I want to be able to start a new session and start tackling everything to build the game'), plus the verb partition that reframes R-05. (1) THE GENERAL SIZE CAPS ARE DELETED, MEASURED RATHER THAN JUDGED. references/atomization_rules.yaml's two CATCH-ALL rules (**/*.md at 15,000 tokens and **/*.yaml at 10,000) carried max_tokens no longer. CLAUDE.md 0.1 pt 5's predicate is the authority (an artifact load-bearing only on this repository's PROCESS can be wrong without cost: delete it, or accept the defect and write nothing), and the caps gated nothing -- advisory, exit 0. RESULT: 116 warnings -> 8, and the 8 are explicit per-file rules, i.e. signal. EVERY EXPLICIT PER-FILE CAP IS UNTOUCHED, including the blocking ones (on_exceed: error on the patch-register archives, block_commit on the session logs). CLAUDE.md SECTION 4 WAS FALSE AND IS CORRECTED: it claimed 'the size cap itself IS enforced, by tools/compliance_check.py'. It never was. Section 9's routing row carried the same claim and is corrected too. What survives is the convention Jordan ruled -- a long document splits into _part2, _part3, ... IN READING ORDER -- now stated as a judgment about whether a reader can work with the file, which is what it always was. (2) THE HANDOFF CAPS ARE LEFT FIRING, DELIBERATELY, AND ANNOTATED. HANDOFF.md is ~16.6k against 4k and HANDOFF_IN.md ~130k against 20k; both are now visible rather than buried. THE OBVIOUS FIX WAS ALREADY TRIED AND REFUSED AND THE REASON BINDS: HANDOFF.md's own 'Next actions' records step 6c ('slim the handoffs') as NOT RUN because its premise ('>=75% of HANDOFF_IN.md is narrative about completed work') measured at 21% corpus-wide, and 'that 21% cannot be swept either: 12 of 17 sections marked [DONE]/[RULED]/EXECUTED carry open, held or needs_jordan items inside them', as does HANDOFF_archive.md. 'The disposition markers in this corpus do not mean what they say. Pruning it is adjudication work, not a culling wave.' So the threshold is NOT raised and the rule is NOT set to skip -- either move converts a standing request for adjudication into a silence. A session began the sweep, read the 6c record, and stopped; that is recorded here rather than silently abandoned. (3) TWO VOCABULARY NOTES, EACH AT BOTH SITES PER CLAUDE.md SECTION 4's 'DEFINE IT IN BOTH PLACES'. Jordan asked both cold and neither was written anywhere. EVENT IS AN ATYPICAL SENSE: ordinary usage and every other engine make an event a thing someone did to someone; here it is neither, by T-d and T-e, and it must be read as 'the occurrence', never 'the message' -- attribution is a per-witness Claim and recipiency is computed at WITNESS from presence. A reader bringing the ordinary sense looks for the actor field, does not find it, and concludes the carrier is incomplete, which is the mistake the three absences exist to prevent. Filed at 01_AXIOMS.md section D.9 (prose) and the Event class docstring in engine/season/state/carriers.py (code). OBSTACLE IS NOT OBSTRUCTION: an obstacle is the difficulty ONE act is resolved against (the Ob, resolver-side, a number, the middle face of ED-IN-0210 Ruling 1's counterparty/obstacle/degree, what contests: routes to); an obstruction is ANOTHER PERSON'S PRIOR ACT REFUSING YOURS (T-g, enforced by a precondition like confer's 1-per-object, carried by emits_on_refusal, needing no verb, no field and no knowledge of the obstructor). An obstacle is rolled against; an obstruction produces a refusal and no degree at all. Filed at T-g (prose) and the verb_table.yaml header (code), which is where the two get confused. (4) THE VERB PARTITION, AND THE TWO ELEVENS ARE DIFFERENT SETS -- a correction to how R-05 reads. requirements.yaml records '11 of 38 verbs execute'; loop/effects.py carries exactly 11 @effect_for bodies; THE OVERLAP IS FIVE. Only create_record, move, release, transfer and utter both EXECUTE and WRITE STATE. Six execute and write nothing (interview, reconstruct, research, speak, surveil, tell -- emit-only), and six have a working effect body no person can reach: confer, convene, destroy_record, revoke (H-71) plus kill / wound and work (the two always-refused, no question refers to a Site). The matching count is a coincidence, and reading the two elevens as one set overstates what runs. CONSEQUENCE THAT MATTERS FOR THE GAME: `tell` executes, declares writes: [], and has no effect body -- so the one verb whose purpose is transmission transmits nothing, which is why 25 driven worlds produce 4,499 claims all stamped firsthand and zero told_by. A witness to a telling learns THAT a telling happened (WITNESS deposits e.kind) and never WHAT was told. (5) A BUILD ORDER WRITTEN INTO ROOT HANDOFF.md, on Jordan's ask, ordered cheapest-game-moving-first: the counterparty (one authored value, controlled 84/0 vs 84/56), tell's effect body, H-71, Ruling 2's six closers, Tenure.term, then the two rulings that are genuinely his. IT IS NOT A BANNER (section 0.3 forbids building one; nothing generates or surfaces it) and it GENERATES NOTHING -- every item traces to a requirement row, a hole-register row, or a ruling Jordan already issued. It also carries what NOT to do, each item costed by a failure that already happened: do not build a guard, do not re-derive a measured hole (H-71 has been independently 'found' twice), do not read the ledger only as code and canon (four of fourteen proposals executed a ruling two days old), do not run the full suite per edit, do not cache a requirement count.

THE PREDICATE, and no marker is trusted -- it reads each unit's BODY, never its title: a unit moved only if it carried NONE of needs_jordan, [OPEN]/STILL OPEN, HELD/SUSPENDED/PARKED/DEFERRED/pause-glyph, BLOCKED, TODO, awaits/awaiting. THE CUT IS AT THE FINEST GRANULARITY THE DOCUMENT ITSELF LABELS, and that is what made it mechanical. 6c's finding is about SECTION headings; the Pending, Decisions and Next actions logs label every ENTRY ([OPEN], [LANDED], [DONE], check-glyph), so those three split per ENTRY and everything else per section. Section-only splitting was tried first and gave IN 130k -> 84k; entry-level gave 72,652, and took MB/PC under cap where section-level left them over. In IN's Pending alone, 30 of 41 entries carried a resolution marker. 'do not' / 'never' WAS DELIBERATELY NOT USED AS A SIGNAL, and this was measured rather than assumed: sampled across the corpus it is ~75% NARRATIVE ('a Date with no due_at is never due', 'never reads a ledger'), and the genuine standing orders are meaningless without the referent their paragraph supplies -- extracting them into a list would reproduce the `evacuate` failure CLAUDE.md section 4 records. Units carrying imperative language are INDEXED AND FLAGGED in the live file instead. ADVERSARIAL CHECK RUN ON THE RESULT: all 8 such moved units in IN were inspected and every one is a prohibition bound to a specific finished artifact ('do not quote the 46 as a finding', 'do not fix it from an IN-lane branch', 'do not skip the critic half'), not a general standing order. That is the check that licenses the move. LOSSLESSNESS IS PROVED, NOT ASSERTED: the line multiset of each live file plus its closed sibling equals the original's exactly. Verified twice -- an in-script assertion, then independently against `git show HEAD:<path>` per lane: 0 lines lost across all four (6,793 + 1,210 + 1,061 + 799 original lines); the only additions are the new headers and indexes. ROOT HANDOFF.md WAS DELIBERATELY NOT SPLIT, on a false positive the dry run caught, and this is the most reusable finding here: THE PREDICATE DETECTS UNRESOLVED-ITEM MARKERS, AND INSTRUCTIONAL CONTENT CARRIES NONE BY NATURE -- it tells you what to do rather than tracking an open item. So the BUILD ORDER written into root HANDOFF.md hours earlier (ED-IN-0220) classified as CLOSED and would have been moved out, along with 'What NOT to do' and 'Known-red on arrival'. Compounding it, root's Next actions mixes dated narrative with SUMMARIES OF JORDAN'S CANON RULINGS (TN 7, universal degree bands, one resolver for d10 probability, DECISIVE_OB is dead); deciding where a ruling record belongs is a judgment call, not a mechanical move. Left alone, with the reason recorded in the file. At ~16.6k it is still readable, which is what IN at 130k was not. ANYONE EXTENDING THIS MUST PIN INSTRUCTIONAL SECTIONS BY NAME FIRST. NO TOOL WAS BUILT, DELIBERATELY. CLAUDE.md 0.1 pt 5's predicate forbids apparatus whose subject is this repository's process, so the splitter was a throwaway script in the session scratchpad and is not in the tree. The deliverable is the split files. The predicate is written into each closed file's header so it can be re-derived by hand. ⚠ THE FALSIFIER ITSELF NEEDED A FIX, FOUND BY ITS OWN NUMBERS NOT MATCHING: its first version always resolved `before` to HEAD^, which on an uncommitted split is one commit too far back, so it compared against a pre-split file that was itself a revision out of date (129,192 instead of 129,964 -- it was missing the HANDOFF_IN append from ED-IN-0218). Now it distinguishes the committed case (parent of the commit that ADDED the closed file) from the uncommitted one (HEAD holds the un-split file). AND THE RULE TENSION THIS EXPOSED, recorded because the resolution is not obvious: CLAUDE.md 0.1 pt 5's predicate says an artifact load-bearing only on process earns no guard, which argued against writing any script at all -- but ED-PC-0040's claim-provenance gate REFUSES a ledger entry stating measured numbers unless it names a re-runnable instrument in the tree, and 0.1 pt 3 requires a result claim to carry the test that would have shown it wrong IN THE SAME COMMIT. Those two are narrower and they win: a ONE-SHOT FALSIFIER IS NOT A GUARD. The script is wired to no CI job and no hook, says so in its own docstring, and says to delete it once the split is old news. Wiring it to CI would convert it into exactly the apparatus the predicate forbids.

description: THE TOLD CHANNEL: `claim_sources` DECLARED FOUR SOURCES AND THE LOOP WROTE ONE. `rosters.yaml: claim_sources` is [firsthand, told_by, inferred, firsthand_via_knot]. MEASURED BEFORE, over the 89 runnable corpus worlds: 23,855 claims, EVERY ONE `firsthand`, 0 `told_by`. `tell` is the one verb whose entire purpose is transmission and it transmitted nothing -- WITNESS deposited `(subject, e.kind, True)`, so a witness to a telling learned THAT a telling happened and never WHAT was told. AFTER: 8 `told_by` claims across 7 of 267 person-instances, each carrying a triple its teller holds and the hearer did not. ⚠⚠ THE FIRST CUT OF THIS UNIT REPORTED 180 AND 134 OF 267, AND THAT NUMBER WAS NEARLY ALL DEFECT. An adversarial pass (read-only, structurally independent per CLAUDE.md section 10) argued the channel was near-vacuous under a co-located fan; measuring its claim rather than accepting it found the sharper fact: **175 of the 180 deposits were a triple the hearer ALREADY HELD FIRSTHAND** -- one belief stored twice, which `loop/witness.py`'s observation block forbids in those words one screen up, each copy taking a `ledger_cap` slot from a claim that would have said something. A guard suppressing an exact-triple redeposit leaves 8, and 8 is the honest size of this channel in this corpus. THE SMALL NUMBER IS THE FINDING. `corpus_run.build_at` seats all three persons in ONE rung, so under `all_five` every observer has already witnessed everything the teller witnessed and there is nothing left to transmit. A corpus of co-located omniscient witnesses cannot exercise transmission -- `W27`'s absent cast arriving from a new direction, not a defect in the channel. AND THE RE-PIN WAS THE DANGEROUS HALF: the first cut moved `test_the_corpus_runs_and_the_ranking_cannot_discriminate` from 25 distinct executed sets to 24 and wrote a derivation for it. The 175 redeposits were what moved the act mix; with the guard the count returns to 25 and the re-pin is REVERTED. A re-pin explaining a defect is worse than a red test. WHERE IT LIVES: `loop/witness.py`, not `loop/effects.py`. An effect body would have to recompute WHO HEARD IT, and the observer fan is this barrier's (`observers_for`) -- a second owner of the observer set is the divergence CLAUDE.md section 8 forbids. `tell` keeps `writes: []` correctly: a telling changes no cell in the world, it changes what people hold. `LedgerReader.latest_about` is added so *the most recent, then the most confident* stays one rule; the subject read goes through `act_refs`, `epistemic`'s own owner, after the first cut re-derived it inline and dropped its bare-string branch (section 8, latent not live, found by the same pass). The teller exclusion is SUBSUMED by the redundancy guard and no longer stated as a second rule -- mutation-testing found that removing it alone reddened nothing, i.e. it could not observe a failure the other guard did not already exclude (section 0.1 pt 2). FALSIFIER, in the tree and mutation-verified: `test_a_telling_deposits_what_was_told_and_the_teller_is_not_told_their_own_news` names the TELLER via the claim id rather than testing 'somebody else holds it', which under a co-located fan is near-tautological -- the same pass showed the old form did NOT redden on the mutation its own docstring named (minting the claim from the Event), because every witness holds that triple. It reddens now. The redeposit assertion lives in the corpus test instead, because `build_world(0)` produces no redeposit and cannot observe that defect. STANDING_OF IS UNMOVED AND CANNOT MOVE FROM THIS SIDE: `agreement` pairs on the `person_predicates` roster (heritage, grade, church_standing, office, residence) and nothing in the loop writes a claim in that vocabulary; `paired == 0` for 267 of 267. ⚠ THE FIRST CUT ATTRIBUTED THIS TO `H-116`, TIER 1. BOTH HALVES WERE WRONG: `H-116` is TIER 0 and is about `belief_contradicts`'s vocabulary, whose read side shipped in `W-A` and write side in `W-B`. The row that owns `standing_of`'s formula and the `person_predicates` pairing is **`H-29`, tier 1, grade `assumption`**, named at `decision/options.py:454` with `site: decision.standing_of / decision.agreement`. Corrected here; the first commit message carries the wrong ID and cannot be edited. ⚠ THE COUNTS ARE EVICTION-CENSORED and the first cut did not say so: they count SURVIVING claims after `ledger_cap`, not deposits, so they can move for reasons unrelated to transmission. MEASURED-BY: engine/season/harness/corpus_run.py -- the `CLAIMS BY SOURCE` line, added by this change because the claim-source tally was a fact about the game no instrument reported, so no number about it was reproducible and `tools/ci_claim_provenance_check.py` correctly refused the entry. Re-run `python -m engine.season.harness.corpus_run`: it prints `{'firsthand': 23849, 'told_by': 8} ... 7 of 267 person-instances hold a `told_by``, plus `DISTINCT EXECUTED SETS 25`. The control (0 `told_by`) is the same command with the `news.told` deposit block removed from loop/witness.py.

THE POPULATED WORLD -- one world, the canonical map, 46 named NPCs, 26 inhabited buildings. Jordan, 2026-09-13: *'I want to see as many persons as there are NPC season loops for each world'*, *'I want there to be multiple locations to inhabit'*, *'each settlement has places/buildings. we need to build these out for testing'*. WHAT IT REPLACES: `corpus_run.build_at` builds ONE WORLD PER CASE and seats exactly three unnamed persons -- p_a, p_b, p_c -- in the SAME rung, in all 89 runnable worlds. MEASURED 2026-09-13: all three act in every world (p_b 2182 acts, p_a 1935, p_c 1911, so it is NOT that one NPC does everything); they are co-located at tick 0 and at the end and NOBODY'S containing rung ever changes in any of the 89; 0 of 4,870 acts name another person; and the told channel (ED-IN-0222) can deposit only 8 second-hand claims corpus-wide because a witness who saw everything the teller saw cannot be told anything. That is `W27`, the absent cast, and it is the stated blocker on R2 and A3. THE LADDER NEEDED NO NEW KIND. `rosters.yaml: rung_kinds` already carries `person < hearth < community < settlement < territory < province < duchy < realm`, and `community` and `hearth` had never been used by any world this repo built -- which is exactly why everyone was in one room, since `build_at` seats a person directly in the settlement. A BUILDING is a `hearth`; a QUARTER is a `community`. Built: 1 realm, 17 provinces, 37 settlements (all canon, read from systems/settlements/valoria_geography_v30.yaml), 60 quarters and 211 buildings (authored, engine/season/venues.yaml), 74 sites, 46 persons in 26 buildings with the largest holding 8. FOUR CORRECTIONS THE BUILD MADE TO ITSELF, each measured rather than reasoned: (1) THE CAST IS 46, NOT 143. The NPC lane names PEOPLE (Carin Vedel, Inge Baralta, Orm); the ARC lane names SITUATIONS (The Unworked Clause, Vaynard's Wager). The first cut seated all 143 and put 97 events in buildings as though they were people, whose 'surnames' (Know, War, Economy, Threshold) then polluted every name match. (2) TITLES ARE NOT NAMES (Jordan: *'inge baralta is Duchess baralta etc. so don't confuse titles with names'*). Matching the full `name:` field finds 11 ties across 9 cases; matching the SURNAME with titles stripped finds 104 across 66. The first number is not a sparse corpus, it is a broken matcher, and reporting it as a finding would have been wrong. (3) THE WANT IS THE CASE'S OWN. The first cut gave all 143 people the string 'a standing ambition' -- `build_at`'s identical-people defect rebuilt at scale. `wants_of` reads the first `core` row of `season_requires`, of which the corpus declares 427 across the 143 cases. (4) A WORLD WITH NO WANTS DOES NOT RUN. Seeded with no Proposition and no `commit`, the populated world completed a full season with **0 acts by 0 actors** -- `questions_for` raises nothing, so every option set is empty. THE TIE IS NEVER A DRAW, in priority order: a person another case NAMES in `who_acts` (12), somebody at the canonical seat of an INSTITUTION the case names (15), a person under the same roof (2), a person in the next inhabited building (17). A draw would read as a relationship and be one only by accident, which is the scripting drift CLAUDE.md section 10 names. THE PROPOSITION SUBJECT IS A PERSON, executing ED-IN-0210 Ruling 1 (*'verbs invoke mechanisms or interactions between a character and another entity/character. they are not fiats'*) -- `world_q`'s Q4 emits `(prop.subject,)` as the referent, which is the whole difference between an act about a granary and an act about somebody. RESULT, 2 seasons: 812 acts by 46 actors, **205 naming another person** against 0 in the entire old corpus, and `told_by` fires. SCOPE: this is a SECOND INSTRUMENT beside `corpus_run`, which still owns grading the 143 cases; nothing here is wired into a gate. What an ARC case IS in this world has no carrier and is named as absent rather than faked. FALSIFIER: `test_the_populated_world_is_not_everybody_in_one_room` -- asserts the cast equals the NPC lane, every ladder level exists, more than one building is inhabited, the largest holds a minority, every person has a want, the wants are distinct, and every Proposition names a person. A bare 'it builds' would pass on a world that seated all 46 in one room. MEASURED-BY: engine/season/harness/populated.py -- run `python -m engine.season.harness.populated 2`, which prints the rung census, the cast size, buildings inhabited, acts by actors, the act-subject split and claims by source. The control is `python -m engine.season.harness.corpus_run`, whose worlds are the three-in-one-room shape this replaces.

THE NPC ROSTER -- `engine/season/npcs.yaml`, generated once and read at runtime. Jordan, 2026-09-13: *'What is the best way to store NPC data? I don't want these NPCs hard-coded into any simulation/test, but pulled in by those scripts'* and *'JSON table or something?'*. WHAT WAS ALREADY RIGHT: the 46 NPCs were never hard-coded -- they come from `engine/season/cases/NPC*.yaml`, read at runtime. WHAT WAS NOT: everything DERIVED about them. Where each lives, what each wants and who each is tied to were computed by regular expressions inside `harness/populated.py` ON EVERY RUN, so a single NPC could not be corrected without editing matcher code, a matcher change moved people with no diff naming who moved, and the roster had no reviewable state. That is CLAUDE.md section 0.05 failing in its usual direction: the mechanism is real and it is in the wrong place. FORMAT DECIDED BY REPOSITORY CONVENTION, NOT PREFERENCE, which answers the JSON question: all seven authored runtime registries in `engine/season/` are YAML (rosters, verb_table, write_matrix, requirements, hole_register, ENDINGS_CLASSIFIED, venues); every JSON artifact in the tree lives under `engine/engine_params/` and is GENERATED, round-trip-checked and port-facing. A hand-edited JSON roster would be the only one in the repository. So: YAML beside the code that reads it. THE DERIVATION IS NOW A BOOTSTRAP, NOT A DEPENDENCY. `build_realm(from_roster=True)` is the default and the matchers are not consulted while the file is present; `from_roster=False` forces the derivation and has exactly one caller -- the exporter, which must not read the file it is about to write. MEASURED: ties read `{roster: 46}` from the file against `{institution: 15, neighbour: 17, roof: 2, named: 12}` derived, and the world runs identically (383 acts, 160 naming another person, 1 season, seed 0). `--check` IS THE ROUND-TRIP AND IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT FAIL ON DRIFT. A hand-corrected home or tie is the file working as intended, and a gate that reddened on one would forbid the very editing the roster exists to allow. It fails only on a row naming a case, a place or a person that does not exist -- which is the anti-fabrication half, and the half worth gating. FALSIFIER, mutation-verified: `test_the_npc_roster_is_read_and_not_merely_shipped` plants a home no matcher would choose and requires the world to honour it; flipping `from_roster` to False reddens it. The failure it excludes is a file nobody opens -- `04 section A.2:124` binds `data/` to RAISE on a declared-but-unread row, `01_AXIOMS.md` ID-13 calls such a thing *'a mechanism that does not exist, wearing a schema's clothes'*, and `rosters.yaml:69-73` records this very file deleting two rosters on that exact criterion. A roster shipped beside a harness that still derived everything would LOOK correct, because the derivation produced it. MEASURED-BY: tools/export_npc_roster.py -- `--build` regenerates the 46 rows from the cases, `--check` re-derives and reports every differing field. `python -m engine.season.harness.populated 1` prints the tie census, which reads `{roster: 46}` when the file is being honoured.

ARCS ARE OUT OF SCOPE. RULED BY JORDAN, 2026-09-13: *'Maybe we just ignore the arcs now.'* WHAT THE QUESTION WAS. The corpus holds 143 cases in two lanes. The NPC lane (46) names PEOPLE -- Carin Vedel, Inge Baralta, Orm -- and ED-IN-0223 seats one person per NPC case in the populated world. The ARC lane (97) names SITUATIONS -- 'The Unworked Clause', 'Vaynard's Wager', 'The Penitent Duke' -- and what an ARC IS in this world has NO CARRIER: no type, no rung, no tenure kind. ED-IN-0223 named that absent rather than inventing one, and listed it as the open design question the populated world did not answer. This closes it: the carrier is not to be built. THE DECISION COSTS NOTHING MEASURABLE, AND THAT IS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The natural worry is that dropping arcs strands half the acceptance bar, since 97 of 143 cases are ARC. It does not. `corpus_run`'s bar reports the ARC lane as **'ENDS = NOT-COMPUTABLE -- closed by W23 (contest results) + W26 (binding decisions) + W30 (the predicates)'**, and an arc CARRIER is on none of those three. The ARC half of the bar was never waiting on this question, and would not start moving if the carrier were built. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, stated because 'ignore the arcs' could be read three ways and only one is meant: the 97 ARC cases are NOT deleted, are NOT excluded from `corpus_run`, and keep being graded exactly as before (R1/R3/R4/R5 per case, the unrepresentable census, the ENDS lane). What is dropped is the DESIGN QUESTION -- 'what is an arc, as a thing the engine holds' -- and with it any obligation on a future session to answer it. `harness/populated.py` continues to seat the NPC lane only, which is what it already did. NO CODE CHANGED. The populated world already excluded ARC cases by construction (ED-IN-0223 corrected an earlier cut that seated all 143 and put 97 events in buildings as though they were people). This row and a note in that module's docstring are the whole of it, because the decision's only cost was a standing open item on an orientation surface, and CLAUDE.md section 0 names closing a settled question with its citation as session work. MEASURED-BY: python -m engine.season.harness.corpus_run -- the two lane headers print the NPC and ARC blockers verbatim; the ARC line names W23/W26/W30 and no carrier.

FLAG CLEARED -- THE ROW IS FULLY DISPOSED AND HAS BEEN SINCE EARLIER TODAY; ONLY THE FIELD WAS STALE. This is bookkeeping with a citation, not a new decision, and it is filed because CLAUDE.md section 0 names exactly this as session work: *'find a stale needs_jordan on a settled question and CLOSE it with its citation. Preserving a dead question is not conservatism; it is how the queue formed.'* THE ROW HELD THREE RULINGS AND ONE FORK, and every one of the four is now accounted for: RULING 1 (*'verbs invoke mechanisms or interactions between a character and another entity/character. they are not fiats'*) -- re-sorted from RULINGS to WORK by ED-IN-0218 section 7.1, and EXECUTED by ED-IN-0223: the populated world gives all 46 NPCs a person-subject Proposition, measured 0 -> 205 acts naming another person. RULING 2 (the six antonym closers) -- re-sorted to WORK by the same amendment; still unbuilt, and unbuilt WORK is not a Jordan gate. RULING 3 ('the six investigation acts' is not a verb) -- executed by ED-FI-0009. THE FORK (*'are dispatch and comply two sides of one thing?'*) -- ANSWERED by ED-IN-0219 on 2026-09-13 under CLAUDE.md section 0 gate 5: NO, they are one producer and one member of the response triad, and the genuinely two-sided pair is dispatch/issue. That row states in its own text that ED-IN-0210 'carried the last live Jordan-gated half of its row' and is 'fully disposed'. WHY THE FLAG SURVIVED ANYWAY: ED-IN-0219 is a SEPARATE id, and the ledgers are append-only with last-row-wins PER ID, so answering a fork in one row cannot clear a field in another. Nothing was wrong except that no row was appended here. That is the mechanism by which this queue accumulates dead questions, and it is worth naming rather than just fixing. THE QUEUE COUNT IS DELIBERATELY NOT STATED HERE, and that is a gate doing its job. The first writing of this row claimed a 35 -> 33 transition and pointed the provenance marker at 'a scan of registers/...' -- prose, not a path, which `ci_claim_provenance_check.py` correctly refused: the marker's whole purpose is that the number can be RE-RUN, and no tool in this tree enumerates the Jordan-gated set. `valoria_master_workplan_v7.md` section 3.5 already records that absence as a `[GAP:]` and says building the enumerator is the reconciled program's work to schedule, not a thing to mint in passing. So the count is omitted rather than asserted with a marker that cannot stand behind it. What this row claims is qualitative and checkable by reading four ids: ED-IN-0218, ED-IN-0223, ED-FI-0009 and ED-IN-0219 dispose of the three rulings and the fork respectively. MEASURED-BY: engine/season/harness/populated.py -- the one transition this row states (0 -> 205 acts naming another person, Ruling 1's execution) is what that module prints on its `act subjects` line; run `python -m engine.season.harness.populated 2`. The control is `python -m engine.season.harness.corpus_run`, whose worlds produce 0. Every other claim here is qualitative and is checked by reading the four ids named above.

THE MILESTONE GATE WAS MEASURING A SUPERSEDED TREE, AND HAS BEEN RE-POINTED AT THE HEAD. Jordan, 2026-09-13, on being told what M1 row 1 was blocked on: *'Remember that mc_v18 is superseded?'* and *'It isn't compliant with Layer 0 or Layer 1?'* -- then *'Let's do 1 now. carefully and comprehensively.'* WHAT WAS WRONG. `tools/m1_acceptance.py` rows 1-2 -- the only rows in the gate that EXECUTE anything -- ran `engine.mc_v18.run_campaign`. Jordan ruled on 2026-09-07 that `engine/season/` IS THE HEAD (HANDOFF_IN.md: '#371 EXISTS ... THE DECOMPOSITION WAS DONE ON THE PROTOTYPE') and ED-IN-0204 adopted the season loop in full, so for six days the milestone gate certified a model the repository had already replaced. WHY THAT IS WORSE THAN A STALE POINTER: CLAUDE.md section 0.2 makes this tool the ONE reading it accepts for 'does the milestone run'. A gate aimed at the wrong tree does not report nothing -- it answers the question it was built to answer, INCORRECTLY, in the direction that looks like progress. Row 1's two failing stub calls were OI-05 and OI-07, deferrals inside code nobody intends to ship; M1 was being held NOT-MET by the prototype's gaps. WHAT CHANGED. Row 1 now takes the delta on `engine.substrate.stubwire.invocations` across a 1-season headless run of the head. Row 2 compares `World.content_hash()` across two same-seed runs. Row 3 was never mc_v18-dependent (it reads module_contracts.yaml statically) and is untouched. MEASURED: rows 1 and 2 both PASS against the head, and the gate's verdict goes from 2 rows failing to 1 -- the survivor being row 4, the DOC-DERIVED board row, which is the row CLAUDE.md already tells readers to treat as bookkeeping. THE QUANTITY IN ROW 2 CHANGED AND THAT IS SAID OUT LOUD, because a re-pointed row that quietly measures something else is a worse defect than a stale one. It compared `KeyLog.content_hash()` and now compares `World.content_hash()`. The new one is STRONGER: `H-118` records that the World hash once covered the log alone and that deleting a person from one of two identical worlds left the hashes matching; it now folds every state collection in sorted-key order ahead of the log. `corpus_run.py:446` already grades its own R4 determinism check with exactly this comparison, so the row reuses an owner rather than inventing one. ROW 1 IS NOT VACUOUS ON THE HEAD, AND THAT IS MUTATION-VERIFIED RATHER THAN ARGUED. The head calls `stubwire` nowhere (`grep -rn stubwire engine/season/` is empty), so a reader is entitled to ask whether the row can still fail. It can: the counter is PROCESS-GLOBAL and the delta spans the whole season, so a stub fired by anything the season reaches is counted. Planting one `stub_resolve` on the head's season path takes the row from 0 PASS to 1 FAIL, and removing it restores 0 PASS. LAYER 0 REPAIRED IN THE SAME CHANGE, which is the part that makes this more than a tool edit. CLAUDE.md section 0.2 itself named 'a seeded engine/mc_v18.py probe' as the milestone's execution artifact. Section 0's rule is that a wrong Layer 0 is repaired BY EDITING THAT FILE, never by routing around it, so the sentence now names the head and carries the incident. SCOPE, STATED BECAUSE THE OBVIOUS NEXT STEP IS NOT TAKEN: `mc_v18` is NOT retired. 71 live files reference it -- the composition spine, the autoload hub, cross-scale dispatch, a BLOCKING round-trip export (`export_composition.py --check`), and 10 files under `engine/tests/` that CI runs as `sim-regression`. Retiring it is its own multi-file piece of work and pretending otherwise inside this change would have broken a blocking job. OI-07 remains open against it. FALSIFIER: `tests/valoria/test_m1_acceptance_probe.py`, 9 tests, including a new `test_the_probe_runs_the_head_and_not_the_superseded_prototype` that asserts the harness module path starts with `engine.season.` and that no `_mc_v18` handle survives -- a property a comment cannot satisfy. MEASURED-BY: tools/m1_acceptance.py -- run `python tools/m1_acceptance.py --summary`; rows 1-2 print the head, the seed and the hash, and the verdict line reads '1 row(s) failing'.

`engine/mc_v18.py` DEPRECATED IN PLACE, AND THE HEAD MADE UNAMBIGUOUS EVERYWHERE A READER LANDS. Jordan, 2026-09-13: *'Make engine/season/ the head. Be comprehensive. Retire mc_v18'*, then -- decisively for the shape this took -- *'We don't have to delete mc_v18 -- we just deprecate it and archive it.'* WHY NOT DELETED, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. Deletion was costed first: **78 of the 136 test functions in `engine/tests/` -- 57% of CI's blocking `sim-regression` job -- import mc_v18**, covering echo transport, the combat bridge seam, parliamentary transfer, accord drift and pipeline reach. Deleting the module first would not have retired a prototype; it would have deleted 78 tests of campaign-scale behaviour and reddened a blocking job in the same commit. The order would have had to be PORT then DELETE. Jordan's ruling removes the need for either. AND `CLAUDE.md` SECTION 1 FORBIDS THE OTHER OBVIOUS MOVE: *'There is no deprecated/ tree ... Do not recreate the directory.'* So 'archive' cannot mean relocating the file, and relocating it would break sixteen importers for no benefit. It is deprecated WHERE IT SITS. THE ENTANGLEMENT IS SMALLER THAN THE GREP SUGGESTED, AND THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING MEASUREMENT. A substring grep finds mc_v18 in 71 live files, which framed this as a large migration. description: THE WRIT AND THE WORD -- document 02 of proposals/2026-09-17-governance-and-holdings-r2/, the round-two centrepiece. PROPOSED, HELD BACK IN FULL. It answers the question ARCH F.15 files as an OPEN GAP: how does authority descend without broadcast? Round one missed that holonic_ARCHITECTURE.md S37.1 ALREADY SPECIFIES the mechanism, by reading S37.3's four prohibitions without the specification above them. Verbatim from S37.1: *'It travels by being noticed, NOT DOWN A CHAIN OF POSTS'*; *'A published dispensation does not apply -- it lands as a compliance contest, per relevant Rung, through `contest`, and SCOPE ENUMERATES EXECUTORS, NOT PLACES'*; *'Delivery is not assumed, and an executor who never received it is DISTINCT from one who received it and refused.'* THE MODEL, shaped by four Jordan rulings of 2026-09-17: TWO PEOPLE-BORNE CHANNELS and MATTER READS NO POLICY AT ALL. The WRIT is a Record of kind `dispensation` minted by `issue`, carried by a person's own `move`, handed over by `give`, arriving VERBATIM OR NOT AT ALL -- its only variance is forgery, copies and destruction. The WORD is `tell`, lossy ONLY at `Partial` on the receiver's Claim, and only by omission or operand drift within a stated band. Jordan's corrections, each of which removed a knob rather than adding one: *'what reaches a hamlet better correspond to some degree what the Duke wrote down… the game can't function as a game where the player can feel their choices mattering if all dissemination of information is so noisy that it's moot'*; *'A document from the Duke isn't like a game of telephone -- the written letter in some form with fidelity would end up being directly given to the settlement leader'*; and *'speed of a writ can be the same as word of it given that the message can be delivered directly as required to those who must implement it'* -- so SPEED IS NOT A DISTINGUISHING AXIS and the two are INDEPENDENT ARRIVALS whose ordering is itself a situation. What a writ buys is fidelity, addressing and EVIDENCE: a physical object that can be produced, checked, forged or destroyed, which is what makes the man holding it the authority on what it says to everyone who cannot read it -- and checkable, at a cost, by someone who travels. ONE DEPOSIT RULE covers commissions, works and petitions alike. NEEDS JORDAN -- RR-P, a CANDIDATE AXIOM. Jordan, verbatim: *'the player must have the sanctity of their choices/actions/decisions preserved in terms of the contents of those choices/actions/decisions themselves -- the worldly churn is in how those contents are received and acted upon by others.'* Stated as THE ACT IS INVIOLATE; THE RECEPTION IS NOT, with the test A DRAW MAY DECIDE WHAT HAPPENS; IT MAY NEVER DECIDE WHAT YOU MEANT, three boundaries (narrowing an option set is legitimate; failure is not corruption; intent reassignment is the forbidden shape), and its existing home in the Act/Claim split. Adoption as AX-7 would bind EVERY subsystem, not only governance, which is why it is escalated rather than assumed. GRADE: paper.

description: SUCCESSOR ROW -- ONE CLAIM IN THE ROW ABOVE IS RETRACTED, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT SOUNDED STRONGEST. That row said valoria-author's no-Bash / no-Agent composition was STRUCTURAL: 'no Bash, so it cannot commit and cannot re-run a 2m36s gate it does not own; and no Agent, so it cannot fan out again'. RULED by Jordan, 2026-09-17, verbatim: 'we still need agents and bash.' Both tools are restored; the definition now holds Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Bash, Agent, and NOTHING IN IT IS A CONTROL -- every rule in the file is one the agent can break, which the file now states in its own first paragraph. WHY THE REFUSAL WAS RIGHT ON MORE THAN ITS OWN TERMS: the first version was INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT. Its own description offered it for 'a code change in a fan-out lane' while removing every means of verifying one -- section 0.4 clause 2's covering test file, section 0.05 clause 3's re-derive-from-the-owner with the repo's tooling, and an exporter's --check round-trip all need Bash. A producer that cannot run the check hands back an unverified edit and moves the work to the orchestrator, which is the opposite of what a fan-out lane is for. THE GENERAL LESSON, recorded in CLAUDE.md section 10 beside the roster because it outlives both agents: REMOVING A TOOL TO ENFORCE A PROCESS RULE BUYS A CONTROL ONLY WHERE THE RULE IS THE ABSENCE. valoria-critic is that case -- 'do not write' and 'holds no write tool' are the same sentence, which is why its independence is structural. 'Do not commit' and 'do not run the full suite' are NOT of that kind: they are cadence rules about WHEN, and a tool removal answers them by deleting the capability rather than the misuse. Those two are now instruction in the file, alongside the positive half section 0.4 actually requires -- DO run the one file covering your edit. AND ONE CONSEQUENCE OF HOLDING BASH IS WRITTEN INTO THE FILE rather than left to be found: the naming guard (tools/hook_naming_guard.py) is wired on the matcher Write|Edit|MultiEdit, so a file rewritten through Bash -- sed, a heredoc, a Python one-liner -- is outside it. CI still catches a deprecated name; the edit-time block is what a shell edit forfeits. THE PATTERN THIS IS AN INSTANCE OF: the first version overreached in the direction that FLATTERS THE AUTHOR -- claiming a structural guarantee is more impressive than claiming a durable instruction, and the row above already warned about exactly this distinction one paragraph before getting it wrong.
